chapter: New Orleans bands, brass bands and learning bass
title: Brass bands and the Zulu parade
summary: Brass bands he played in, how the Zulu parade began with coal-yard workers and a mule, and second-liners collecting money to hire a band for a funeral.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: What brass bands did you play with then?
Uh huh. Any others? Did you ever play for the Zaloons?
I rang you when they organized that thing, Padilla and Liberty.

Yeah, I don't know. Kids start that. Little, uh, Sash Moe. Little, little, little, little. Guy, them fellas work out there for W.C. Kyle's a coal yard. Used to drive them dump carts, coal carts, you know? Uh huh. Used to land, let them have a mule, you know? They have a mule. Put in the parade for the Zulus, you know? Uh huh.
And Mr. Janky had a lot of them working for him, didn't he?
Oh yeah. I think he sure did. He used to toast them.
Remember when he toasted them in champagne? Was that during your time? Uh huh. Must have been fun of Zulus.
And then if I, uh, if God died, one of the boys, uh, and the gang would pass. You know these days, they'd start hustling around, collecting, getting the money to have a band.

All the second lines that come in, anybody that catch it, put a quarter or fifteen cents, you know? Make up with the one to get a band. And they say band, they'll, they'll sure come up with some change, alright.
